text.title: Freelancer Rate Raise Letter Template Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete rate-raise artefact for a EUR 6,000 monthly retainer raised 12% with a 62-day grace period, the 196-word letter it describes, a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad artefact showing what the validator and the reviewer reject.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Acme Analytics has been on a EUR 6,000 per month retainer since July 2025. Since March 2026 the freelancer owns the release pipeline Acme previously paid an agency for, and deploy lead time fell from nine days to one. The MSA's clause 9.3 requires 30 days' notice of a rate change; the retainer bills monthly. Acme is 18% of trailing-12-month revenue. The quarterly review is on 2026-07-01.

example.title: Acme retainer, +12% effective 2026-09-01
example.note: `effective_date` is 62 days out, not 30: the retainer bills monthly and the July-August period is prepaid, so the first clean cycle at the new rate is September. That is the longest of 30 days, one full cycle and the clause 9.3 notice period (r-grace-period-at-least-30-days).

Two value deltas, both citing `engagement-log-q1-q2`: the agency line Acme no longer pays (EUR 2,400 per month, more than triple the EUR 720 increase) and a metric with before and after. No CPI sentence at all (r-justify-with-value-delta-not-cpi).

One number: 6720, with 6000 beside it and 12%. The prepared concession (rate held to year-end against a prepaid six months) is in the artefact and nowhere in the letter (r-single-new-rate-stated, r-no-concession-in-the-letter).
`churn_risk.class` is `negotiate` because Acme has a real alternative at 2x cost; at 18% of revenue no replacement plan is required (r-churn-risk-classified-before-send).

Dana confirmed in writing on 2026-07-06, before the follow-up date; `new_rate_applied` stays false until the 2026-09-01 invoice, and the follow-up path for `confirmed` (send the clause 9.3 variation for signature) is what happens next (r-follow-up-at-t-plus-7-with-path).

example.title: The 196-word letter the artefact describes
example.code:
Subject: Retainer rate from 1 September 2026
Dana,
Since March I have owned Acme's release pipeline end to end, the work you previously paid an agency for, and deploy lead time has gone from nine days to one. That is the basis for this note.
From 1 September 2026 my monthly retainer moves from EUR 6,000 to EUR 6,720, a 12% change. Everything already agreed stays as it is: SOW-2026-03 (the warehouse migration) completes at the current rate, and the prepaid July-August retainer period is unaffected. The new rate applies only to work agreed from September.
Clause 9.3 of our MSA asks for 30 days' notice of a rate change; this letter gives 62, so the September invoice is the first at the new rate and no invoice mixes the two.
I will follow up on 8 July. If you can confirm before then, I will send the updated retainer schedule for signature so finance has it well ahead of September.
Ruslan
example.note: Opens with the value delivered, states one number with the old rate and percentage, protects the in-flight work by name, closes with the effective date and the follow-up date. No apology, no costs story, no fallback (r-business-notice-tone-no-apology).

example.title: What the validator and the reviewer reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.rate.is_range_or_open: must equal False, got True`, `$.schedule.days_to_effective: 0 violates minimum=30`, `$.schedule.billing_cycles_to_effective: 0 violates minimum=1`, `$.schedule.scope_change_documented_at: missing required field`, `$.justification.value_deltas: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.justification.cpi_or_costs_is_sole_justification: must equal False, got True`, `$.letter.word_count: 410 violates maximum=250`, `$.letter.opens_with_value_delivered: must equal True, got False`, `$.letter.states_protected_work: must equal True, got False`, `$.letter.closes_with_effective_and_follow_up_dates: must equal True, got False`, `$.letter.banned_phrases_found: 2 items, maxItems=0`, `$.letter.personal_cost_narrative: must equal False, got True`, `$.letter.concession_in_letter: must equal False, got True`, `$.prepared_concession.use_only_in_follow_up: must equal True, got False`, `$.churn_risk.replacement_revenue_plan: missing required field`, `$.follow_up.days_after_letter: must equal 7, got 45`, `$.acknowledgement.received_on: missing required field`, `$.acknowledgement.received_in_writing: must equal True, got False`.

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: `inputs_used` carries a CPI table and no engagement log, so no value delta could ever be cited (r-justify-with-value-delta-not-cpi); the follow-up paths are not paths, and two of them invoice on silence (r-follow-up-at-t-plus-7-with-path); a 42%-of-revenue client with "usually late" payment behaviour and no alternatives analysis is being raised blind (r-churn-risk-classified-before-send).
